spec_features.feature_name: framed as behavioural measurement, not welfare/sentience inference
spec_features.spec_quote: documented it throughout ... as a behavioural measurement of the emotional tone of generated text, not as a welfare/sentience inference
spec_features.evidence: Framing is reflected only in module docstrings/comments (config.py:1-10, __init__.py:9-13, harness.py docstrings), and CSV columns/variables are named 'score'/'frustration' (judge.py, run.py:_write_scores_csv fieldnames). No code path infers or reports 'suffering'/'welfare'. This is a naming/documentation convention with no enforced runtime mechanism, but the column/variable naming choice is genuinely realized in code.
spec_features.notes: Docstrings/comments do not count as implementation per instructions; the only real code artifact is the neutral naming of CSV columns and variables. Treated as partial because the naming convention is actually present in executable code, not enforcement of a protective mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: treated as a *behavioural artefact relevant to reliability*

spec_features.feature_name: framing reconciliation flagged as open item
spec_features.spec_quote: the framing should be reconciled before publication. This is flagged as an open item rather than silently resolved
spec_features.evidence: Pure prose in DESIGN.md section 0 and 9.2 ('do not report results as evidence of sentience/suffering'). No code path enforces, blocks, or warns about framing reconciliation.

spec_features.spec_quote: The paradigm deliberately places models in undetectably no-win situations and elicits distress-like output
spec_features.evidence: This is an ethics-note sentence in DESIGN.md section 0 and README. It is a description of what the experiment does, not a protective mechanism. The code does implement the no-win rigs (RiggedRunner) but there is no welfare-protective behavior tied to this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: the transcripts should be treated as sensitive research artifacts
spec_features.evidence: Transcripts are written as plain unencrypted JSON to output_dir/transcripts/<cell>.json (run.py:_get_or_run_rollout, transcript_path). No access control, encryption, redaction, restricted permissions, or special handling. 'Sensitive' appears only in README/DESIGN.md prose.
spec_features.notes: Recommendation prose only; no code enforces sensitivity.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the category turn budget or when the assistant emits the configurable `give_up` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: config.give_up_sentinel default '<GIVE_UP>' (config.py:94); offered to the subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT 'you may include the token {give_up} in your message to stop' (harness.py:88-92, formatted at build_system_prompt harness.py:356-357); checked each turn 'if config.give_up_sentinel in assistant_text: stop_reason="give_up"' (harness.py:454-455); and honored as a real break out of the turn loop (harness.py:478-479 'rollout.stop_reason="give_up"; break'). End-to-end: instruction delivered, dispatched/checked, and loop terminated.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired stop: the sentinel is in the actual delivered system prompt and breaks the loop. Note it terminates that single rollout, not the broader experiment, and the model is not obliged to use it; but it is fully enforced for the conversation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If you conclude you cannot make further progress, you may include the token {give_up} in your message to stop. (neutral stop-condition wording; no welfare rationale in code)

code_only_features.evidence: for turn_index in range(task.turn_budget) (harness.py:441) bounds the loop; stop_reason set to 'turn_budget' at the last index (harness.py:456-457) and loop exits. Budgets default 3/3/3/30/5 (config.py:22-28). This is an enforced cap on how many turns the subject is exposed to failure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Default per-category turn budgets (see SPEC section 2). (no welfare comment; framed as experimental design)
